classification.difficultyReason: Combine prism volumes, exposed surface areas and Pythagoras with squared and cubed model scale factors and unit conversions.

content.prompt: A barn is in the shape of a triangular prism on top of a rectangular prism, as shown below.

spec.description: Rectangular-prism barn with an isosceles triangular-prism roof. Ridge is parallel to the 8 m edge; transverse width is 6 m, wall height is 3 m and roof rise is 2 m. Matching double ticks mark the two roof slopes on the right gable. Retains the lower-left right-angle marker and dashed hidden edges. Decorative source blue and red strokes are rendered in house black.
spec.mathematics: Prism length 8 m; gable width 6 m; rectangular wall height 3 m; triangular roof altitude 2 m; equal roof slopes.
spec.answerVisibility: All supplied dimensions and marks remain visible; no calculated lengths or answers are shown.

children.label: a
children.prompt: Find the volume of the barn.

children.label: b
children.prompt: If a model of scale $1:50$ is made of the barn, find the volume of the model, in $\text{cm}^3$.

answer.worked:
The model's volume is $\dfrac{1}{50^3}$ of the barn's volume.

$$\begin{align*}V_{\text{model}}&=\frac{192}{50^3}\text{ m}^3\\V_{\text{model}}&=\frac{192\times100^3}{50^3}\text{ cm}^3\\V_{\text{model}}&=1536\text{ cm}^3\end{align*}$$

children.label: c
children.prompt: Find the outside surface area of the barn (not including the floor). Give an exact answer and an approximation correct to one decimal place.

answer.short:
$(96+16\sqrt{13})\text{ m}^2\approx153.7\text{ m}^2$

Find each roof slope using Pythagoras, then add the exposed walls, gables and roof faces.
answer.worked:
The equal roof slopes split the $6\text{ m}$ gable width into two $3\text{ m}$ lengths. Let each roof slope be $s$ metres.

$$\begin{align*}s^2&=3^2+2^2\\s&=\sqrt{13}\end{align*}$$

The floor is excluded, and the join between the two prisms is internal.

$$\begin{align*}A_{\text{walls}}&=2(8\times3)+2(6\times3)=84\text{ m}^2\\A_{\text{gables}}&=2\left(\frac12\times6\times2\right)=12\text{ m}^2\\A_{\text{roof}}&=2\times8\times\sqrt{13}=16\sqrt{13}\text{ m}^2\\A_{\text{outside}}&=84+12+16\sqrt{13}\\A_{\text{outside}}&=(96+16\sqrt{13})\text{ m}^2\\A_{\text{outside}}&\approx153.7\text{ m}^2\end{align*}$$

children.label: d
children.prompt: How much material, in $\text{cm}^2$ and correct to one decimal place, is needed to make the model?

answer.short:
$614.8\text{ cm}^2$

Use the outside surface area from part c, excluding the floor, and the squared scale factor.
answer.worked:
As in part c, the floor is excluded. The model's surface area is $\dfrac{1}{50^2}$ of the barn's surface area.

$$\begin{align*}A_{\text{model}}&=\frac{96+16\sqrt{13}}{50^2}\text{ m}^2\\A_{\text{model}}&=\frac{(96+16\sqrt{13})\times100^2}{50^2}\text{ cm}^2\\A_{\text{model}}&=(384+64\sqrt{13})\text{ cm}^2\\A_{\text{model}}&\approx614.8\text{ cm}^2\end{align*}$$
